description:
Deep analysis of `OctoPi.TUI.Interactive` (`apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/interactive.ex`) identified five structural issues in the rendering/event pipeline. All five should be resolved before heavier feature work on Interactive.

## The five issues

**Issue 1 — Three `handle_info` clauses bypass `handle_event` entirely.**
The module docstring (L10–15) establishes that `handle_event/2` is the canonical pure state machine and that tests can drive it directly. Three `handle_info` clauses mutate state inline and call `advance` directly, without going through `handle_event`:
- `:force_render` (L502–504)
- `{:extension_result, text}` (L493–495)
- `{:custom_done, from, result}` (L497–499)

Any future per-event logic (tracing, hooks, testing) added to the handle_event path is silently skipped for these three.

**Issue 2 — `handle_call` skips `maybe_suspend` / `maybe_launch_editor`.**
`advance/1` (L631–638) runs `maybe_suspend` + `maybe_launch_editor` + `render_frame`. `handle_cast({:ui_fire, ...})` (L557–560) calls `advance`, so it drains pending side effects. But `handle_call({:ui_request, msg})` (L541–554) calls `render_frame` directly, skipping both. `suspend_pending` and `editor_pending` are only ever set by key-event handlers today, so this is not currently observable — but it is a latent correctness trap: any future `handle_ui_request` clause that sets those flags would silently fail to fire.

**Issue 3 — `Renderer.resize` lives in `handle_info`, not in `render_frame`; causes a notification-clear bug.**
Resize is the only event whose `handle_info` clause makes a peer GenServer call before delegating to `handle_event`:
```elixir
def handle_info({:hid_event, %Resize{width: w, height: h} = event}, state) do
  Renderer.resize(state.renderer, w, h)      # ← peer call here
  state |> handle_event(event) |> advance()
end
```
This special-case clause intercepts `{:hid_event, %Resize{}}` before the generic `{:hid_event, event}` clause (L480–485), which contains `Map.put(:notification, nil)`. Result: resize events never clear `state.notification`. A visible notification persists through a terminal resize.

**Issue 4 — Unreachable dead code in `handle_ui_request`.**
Lines 282–284 define a clause:
```elixir
def handle_ui_request(state, {:custom, _factory, _opts}) do
  {state, :pending}
end
```
This is unreachable. `handle_call/3` at L531 has a specific clause for `{:ui_request, {:custom, ...}}` that always intercepts first and never calls `handle_ui_request`. The dead clause creates a false impression of an alternate `:custom` handling path.

**Issue 5 — `advance/1` conflates three concerns.**
`advance/1` bundles: (1) flushing pending TTY side effects, (2) rendering, (3) producing the OTP return tuple. A `flush_effects/1` helper needs to exist independently so both `advance` and `handle_call` can use it (required to fix issue 2).

## Subtickets and order of operations

- **Ticket 1** (dead code): independent, no blockers.
- **Ticket 2** (notification/resize): independent, no blockers.
- **Ticket 3** (extract flush_effects): independent, no blockers.
- **Ticket 4** (bypass paths through handle_event): independent, no blockers.
- **Ticket 5** (handle_call uses flush_effects): **blocked by ticket 3** — flush_effects must exist first.
- **Ticket 6** (Renderer.resize into render_frame): **blocked by ticket 2** — notification fix must be in `handle_event(%Resize{})` before the special-case `handle_info` clause is removed.

All changes are in `apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/interactive.ex`. Run `mix test apps/octo_pi_tui/` to validate each ticket.
title: Interactive render-path cleanup: consolidate event dispatch and effect execution
